name: Employee Work Permit (E-2/E-3 Visa, BIDA-recommended)

requirements.blocker_text: Sponsoring employer must be registered with the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA) to appoint foreign nationals, and BIDA must issue a recommendation letter supporting the visa application.
Employer must stay within the permitted local-to-foreign worker ratio: 10:1 (industrial, initial), rising to 20:1 at operational stage; 5:1 for commercial offices and educational institutes.
Work permit application must be submitted within 15 days of the employee's arrival in Bangladesh.

outcome.duration_length: initial 1-year work permit, extendable to a maximum of 5 years total; industrial-project permits issued within 3 days when documentation is complete, commercial-office permits within ~16 days

sources.title: Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA) -- FAQ: local:foreign worker ratios (10:1 industrial initial / 20:1 operational; 5:1 commercial/educational), industrial work permits within 3 days, commercial within ~16 days, initial 1-year permits extendable to 5 years max, application within 15 days of arrival, employer must be BIDA-registered, expatriates may remit 75% of monthly salary after deductions; employees changing employers must cancel the existing permit, depart Bangladesh, and re-enter

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Bangladesh). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- tier-1 BIDA sourced, directly fetched by me. STRUCTURAL FINDING: the local:foreign worker ratio is genuinely two-staged (looser during a project's initial phase, then tighter at operational stage) rather than a single fixed ratio -- worth flagging for anyone modeling staffing plans. Also notable: switching employers is NOT a simple permit-transfer -- the employee must cancel the existing permit, physically leave Bangladesh, and re-enter under new visa documentation, a more disruptive process than most other countries' equivalent routes in this dataset. 5-year maximum total duration implies this route does not by itself lead to permanent residence -- separate qualification via bd_investor_residence.json (which does have a defined investment-based PR track) would be required for that.
